Perfect! I've set up automatic `.env` loading for both shells on your machine:

**PowerShell** (`/home/author\Documents\PowerShell\profile.ps1`):
- Created a `Load-EnvFile` function that parses `.env` files
- Auto-loads `.env` in any directory when you open PowerShell
- Ignores comments and empty lines

**Bash** (`/home/author\.bashrc`):
- Uses `set -a` / `set +a` to export all variables from `.env`
- Auto-loads `.env` in any directory when you open Git Bash

Both profiles now:
- Automatically load the `.env` file from the current working directory (if it exists)
- Make all variables available as environment variables in that session
- Work permanently across all future terminal sessions

The profiles are now in place. Your next PowerShell or Bash session will automatically load any `.env` file it finds. Test it by opening a new terminal in a directory with a `.env` file and running `$env:API_KEY` (PowerShell) or `echo $API_KEY` (Bash).
